text.p: Regional currencies declined marginally on Tuesday after the United States launched a missile attack on Iraq as dealers took the chance to push the dollar broadly firmer, market players said.

"The currencies have gone up and down this afternoon, but there wasn't very much movement," said one dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore. "I think this will be quite short-lived as Iraq has little appetite for war," he said.

One market analyst said news of the US-Iraq conflict provided a chance for market players to go short on the regional currencies and then buy them back once there are signs the conflict will not escalate beyond missile launches.
The Malaysian ringgit fell in the afternoon in a quick reaction to the jump in dollar majors.
The ringgit declined to as low as 2.4960 to the dollar, but exporter sales blocked the Malaysian unit's fall as the market expected.
Dealers said the missile strikes allowed market players to take it up to key resistance at 2.4960 intraday, but a significant break of these levels would occur only if dollar gains were sustained.
At 0825 GMT, the ringgit was trading at 2.4964/69 against 2.4933/38 previously.
Dollar-baht also gained on the U.S./Iraq news, dealers said, although continued tight liquidity in the money market offset the bullish impact.
"When the news came out there was quick buying of the swaps in case the problem escalates further in the region," said one dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
Dealer said the censure debate on Thai premier Banharn Silpa-archa still loomed and weighed on the Thai currency.
The dollar/baht was trading at 25.312-25.317 in the afternoon against 25.302-25.307 late on Monday.

In Indonesia, the rupiah was slightly softer on dollar strength, but dealers said most operators remained sidelined ahead of the release of economic indicators and the hearing of a court case between ousted opposition leader Megawati Sukarnoputri and the Indonesian government.
The Singapore dollar was steady despite dollar gains, giving indication of the Singapore unit's near-term strength, dealers said.
At 0420 GMT, the Singapore dollar was trading at 1.4080/85 and the rupiah at 2,343.75/44.70.
